answer: Add/Drop Groups are managed with add/set/show/delete adg-<adg-number>. The adg-number is an integer in the range [1..110], matching oadm-capabilities max-adgs of 110, so a node supports up to 110 ADGs. Duplicate wavelengths are governed by the read-only show attribute wavelength-duplication, which has two values: one-per-adg (no duplication of frequencies in the ADG) and one-per-degree (CDC: duplication of frequencies allowed in the ADG, but only one at the Degree). The default is one-per-adg, and only CDCs allow more than one instance of the same wavelength on the ADG. Other attributes: label (String 0..256), max-add-drop-ports (show, integer) and bands-supported, default standardC-band.

On set amplifier-<name>, gain-target is used for constant-gain mode and takes 0..40 dB, default 0.0; it applies only when control-mode is manual. control-mode is auto-max-pw (default, auto mode targeting maximum output power) or manual, and amp-control-support says whether auto-max-pw is even permitted (auto, or manual-only). In auto mode you bias the system value with gain-adjustment, range [-20.00..20.00], default 0, supported only on amplifiers whose function is pa or inline. Tilt is controlled by tilt-control-mode: auto (default, system controls tilt from configured fiber parameters), auto-planned (per planning tool parameters) or manual; when the amplifier function is add or drop, only manual is possible. tilt-target ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) applies in manual mode and raises a traffic-affecting warning; tilt-adjustment ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) offsets the auto/auto-planned target, and tilt-actual reports the measured tilt.

Use set amplifier-raman-<name> target-raman-gain <value>. The range is [0, 5..30dB] with default 0dB. It is configurable only when control-mode is different from auto; in control-mode auto the parameter is ignored. control-mode values are auto (default, you configure only span attributes), auto-planned (you configure the target Raman gain plus span attributes) and manual (even the amplifier target pump powers must be configured). Pump count is read from show amplifier-raman-<name> number-of-pumps, whose values are 4 or 2; that value dictates how many pump-power objects the system exposes. Related read-only values are total-pump-power ([-99..99 dBm], -99 means no power), actual-raman-signal-gain and actual-raman-osc-gain.

Turn it on with set ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-enable enabled, for example set ase-idler-service-1-8 ase-idler-enable enabled. ase-idler-enable takes enabled or disabled and defaults to disabled; enabled means ASE idler signal filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum is enabled. The entity can also be created or removed with add/delete ase-idler-service-<name>, and add/set accept alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited). To see whether it came up, read the show-only ase-idler-state: ase-enabled (filling complete on the band spectrum), ase-partially-enabled (filling incomplete), ase-faulted (idler signal faulted) or ase-disabled (default, signal completely removed). oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and function (idler) are also shown.

On set ase-idler-source-<name>, target-output-power is the ASE pump output power required when manually configured; its range is (-3.00..20.50) dBm and the default is 13. The pump is not on by default: pump-enable takes enabled or disabled with default disabled, and the read-only pump-state (enabled/disabled) also defaults to disabled. Example from the guide: set ase-idler-source-1-3.1-ase pump-enable 'enabled' target-output-power '15.00'. Other settable attributes are admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), label (0..256) and alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited). function is fixed at ase-idler-source and oper-state defaults to disabled.

Use the calibrate command, which runs in Operational Mode only: calibrate [type=]<value> [trigger=]<value> [entity=]<value>. type has one value, raman, which triggers calibration on raman cards. trigger is start (starts the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span) or stop (stops it). entity is an instance-identifier selecting the object to calibrate; for raman calibration the entity may be an OTS-R entity. To start: calibrate raman start ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line. To stop: calibrate raman stop ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line. There is no default for any of the three parameters.

Degrees are created with add degree-<degree-number>, where degree-number is an integer in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees; oadm-capabilities reports max-degrees of 20. Spectral granularity is read from show degree-<degree-number>: slot-width-granularity is the width of a slot, default 6250 (value in MHz), and center-freq-granularity is the granularity of allowed center frequencies, default 3125 MHz, computed from a base frequency of 193.1 THz per G.694.1. A media channel is built from between min-slots (default 8) and max-slots (default 32) slots joined together. Other show attributes are is-foadm (default false), wss-less (default true) and bands-supported (default standardC-band).

The pairing is automatic. Direction n and direction n+1 are assigned by the system to the DWDM Line1 and DWDM Line2 ports of the #n C2ILASGH/D2ILASGM card created, where index n is an odd integer with a value between 1 and 15. DWDM Line1 is always assigned an odd index value and DWDM Line2 always an even one. The direction index range is [1..16] (1 and 2 are used when migrating from R6.x). The system sets direction-number from the configured direction-port: 1 when the port is dwdm-line1, 2 when it is dwdm-line2, so odd indexes carry direction-number 1 and even indexes direction-number 2. It also fills direction-card as card-<chassis>-<slot>. The same dwdm-line* port instance of an ILAx can only be selected once per NE. Syntax: add direction-<index> direction-port <value> [label <value>]; delete [-f] forces without confirmation.

The dsc facility supports add/delete/set/show dsc-<name>. The user-configurable attributes are just three: label (String 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed, the default, or inhibited). Everything else is read-only on show: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by. managed-by describes whether this facility was system created or not; its values are system (the default) and user. It matters operationally because only user-created facilities can be user deleted, so a dsc reporting managed-by system cannot be removed with delete.

On add/set dsc-group-<name> the pre-FEC pair is pre-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold, decimal64 with 3 fraction digits, range 0|5.600..9.600 dB, which raises the PRE-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE alarm; setting 0 disables threshold-crossing alarming, and the usable sub-range is per carrier use-case. Its companion pre-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. The post-FEC pair is post-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold, decimal64 with 1 fraction digit, range 12.5..18.0 dB, default 18, raising POST-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE, and post-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis, range 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. A related degrade threshold is dgd-high-threshold, uint16 in the range 25..400 ps, default 100, which raises the DGD-OORH alarm.

Use the gadt command (Golden Application Description Table): show gadt [<application-description-H|application-description-P|application-description-S|application-description-U>]. It retrieves information about golden carrier application information, and the four parameters are each a detailed description of an application ID (H, P, S and U), all of type string with no default. It runs in both Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For example, show gadt application-description-H returns application-description 'Subsea modes using Uniform and Hybrid modulation'. The application IDs shown here are the same ones that appear in the application field of a golden carrier mode.

gapt lists the golden advanced parameters from the Golden Advanced Parameters Table. The syntax is show gapt-<card-type> [version] [applicable-resource-type], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. It is scoped per card type: card-type is a string, so the table instances appear as gapt-CHM6, gapt-CHM7, gapt-CHM7T and so on, and a bare show gapt lists them with their version and applicable-resource-type columns. version is a string of length 0..5 (for example 1.8 or 3.0) and applicable-resource-type is a string naming the managed resource type(s) applicable for that advanced parameter. Scoping to one card, for example show gapt-chm7, lists that card's entries as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/<name>, such as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/NLC or /RxCDMode.

Use the gcmt command, which retrieves information about the golden carrier mode: show gcmt [<card-type>] [version], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Its parameters are object (the golden carrier modes, string) and version (the table version, string). To look up one mode, name it directly: show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P. The output lists golden-carrier-mode golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P with capacity (Gbps) 800, client-mode ethernet-otn, baud-rate (GBaud) 95.2965203, application P, compatibility-id 6 and status supported. For the full per-attribute view of one mode, use show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode>.

Read the status attribute: show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> status. status describes the carrier mode release status and its values are supported, candidate, experimental, deprecated and diagnostic, so a mode is fully supported only when status reads supported, and an experimental mode reports experimental. The same status column also appears in show gcmt output. Two related attributes qualify per-subtype maturity: supported-subtypes lists the subtypes each carrier mode supports (string 0..32, maximum 20 elements), and candidate-subtypes lists the subtypes for which this carrier mode has candidate status (string 0..16, maximum 10 elements). The command also returns actual-carrier-mode, capacity, client-mode (ethernet or ethernet-otn), baud-rate, application, compatibility-id and sop-tracking-mode.

The l0-capabilities command shows the capabilities details related with the node's Layer 0 functions. The syntax is simply show l0-capabilities, it takes no parameters at all, and it is available in both Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For the OADM-specific limits underneath it, use show oadm-capabilities, which reports max-degrees (20) and max-adgs (110), and for per-degree spectrum granularity use show degree-<degree-number> (slot-width-granularity, center-freq-granularity, min-slots, max-slots, bands-supported).

A Media Channel is created with add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [auto-delete <value>]. The three mandatory inputs are parent-oms, lower-frequency and upper-frequency; the two frequencies are values in MHz. parent-oms is an instance-identifier that is only set upon MC creation, and its referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree, it cannot be in an ADG. The system derives center-frequency (MHz) and slot-width, calculated as upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. auto-delete defaults to disabled; when enabled the system auto-deletes the MC once its associated NMC is deleted, and it is only allowed on RD66TM sleds (l0-mode-op=hsc-ols), always disabled if l0-mode-op is standard or slte. Example: add mc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 parent-oms '1-3.1-dwdm-line' lower-frequency '192225000' upper-frequency '192300000'.

The Media Channel Filler is read only. The mc-f command supports show only: show mc-f-<name> [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [AID] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [slot-width]. There is no add, set or delete form. The displayed attributes are name (String 0..64), supporting-facilities and supported-facilities (instance identifiers to the parent and children facilities), supporting-card and supporting-port (leafrefs to the card and port that hold the facility), AID (String 1..64), lower-frequency and upper-frequency of the MC Filler in MHz units, and slot-width, calculated by the system from upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. It is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. By contrast the network media channel filler, nmc-f, does allow set of admin-state and alarm-report-control.

Up to four cards. The syntax is add modules-adg-<adg-number>/<index> supported-card <value> [ocm-monitoring <value>], where adg-number is a number in the range [1..110] and index is a number in the range [1..4]. The card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is an instance identifier for the card being placed in the ADG. Channel monitoring is on by default: ocm-monitoring defaults to true. It is set upon creation and cannot be changed after supported-card has been assigned, but it can optionally be configured to false for OMD cards directly connected to PAx/BAX or C2ILASGH degrees, for example FOADM nodes. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, privilege Network Administrator or Network Engineer. Example: add modules-adg-1/1 supported-card card-1-6.

Use the modules-degree command: add modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>. degree-number is a number in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. Unlike an ADG, a degree has only one module index: index is 1, and the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is an instance identifier of the card or subcard that belongs to the degree; in R6.0 the card must be RD09SM or RD20TM. The same command supports set modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> [supported-card <value>], show and delete. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode, privilege Network Administrator or Network Engineer. Example: add modules-degree-1/1 supported-card card-1-1.

Use show monitored-channel-<name>/<frequency> monitored-optical-power. The name corresponds to the (WS04S) card name with the suffix -1 or -2, for ocm1-in or ocm2-in respectively, and frequency is the nominal center frequency of the carrier in MHz (uint32). monitored-optical-power is the measured power for that carrier in dBm, decimal64 in the range (-99.00..99.00) with default -99, where -99.00 means no power. The command also returns monitored-width, a uint32 in MHz with default 0, which is the carrier width configured at the NMC within the oxcon source or destination. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. Example: show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 monitored-optical-power.

On add nmc-<name>, center-frequency is mandatory and takes values in the range [190650000..196700000] MHz. The optional width is the Network Media Channel frequency width in MHz, with values in the range [15000..200000] MHz and a default of 35000. The guide states the user must configure the 3 dB signal bandwidth, and that the value in GHz must be equivalent to the baud rate in GBd configured on the connected transponder line interface line port. Both center-frequency and width are set at creation (add) and are read back with show; they are not in the set list. The other mandatory creation input is parent-facility, which can be either a Media Channel or an OMS, is only set upon creation, and whose referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree and cannot be in an ADG. Example: add nmc-cdc-1-4_192800000-34000 center-frequency 192800000 width 34000 parent-facility oms-1-4-ad1.

The Network Media Channel Filler occupies a default allocated bandwidth of 75000 MHz: alloc-bandwidth is a value in MHz units with default 75000, bounded by alloc-lower-frequency and alloc-upper-frequency. What is actually in use is reported separately by actual-bandwidth (MHz, default 0) with actual-lower-frequency and actual-upper-frequency. Yes, it is monitored: monitoring-state indicates whether the NMC is intended to be in use, its values are enabled and disabled, and because it is a system created attribute it is enabled by default. Powers are reported by power-actual-tx and power-actual-rx, both [-99.00..99.00] dBm with default -99, plus output-attenuation-compensation-actual (decimal64, 2 fraction digits, range -20..20, default 0). Only admin-state and alarm-report-control are settable via set nmc-f-<name>.

Use show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs], available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees, reported as 20 (uint8), and max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups, reported as 110 (uint8). Either reads 0 if not supported: degrees and ADGs are only supported in OADM node types, and the maximum degrees for ILA node-type is 0 by convention because an ILA has only 2 directions, fixedly, which is not shown in supported capabilities. Note that the maximum number of Degrees is not necessarily the deployment supported configuration, but the maximum number of a working degree-number. Sample output shows max-degrees 20 and max-adgs 110. These match the degree-number range [1..20] and adg-number range [1..110].

On set oc-<name>, loopback takes facility, terminal or none, defaulting to none, and is useful to debug on the fiber connection; loopback-mode indicates the loopback action for facility or terminal and takes facility or terminal with no default. For test patterns, test-signal-type is the type of test pattern that is injected, with values none, enumeration, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9 and PRBS31, defaulting to none. test-signal-direction has the single value ingress, which is also the default. test-signal-monitoring monitors the incoming test signals for diagnostics and takes true or false, defaulting to false. Example: set oc-1-5-T9.1 test-signal-monitoring false. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

In ILA nodes the OCHm represents the signaled optical channel from OSC, detected at the ILA OMS by using the OSC information. The list of ochm facilities in an NE will be empty when either the OMS monitoring-mode is not-monitored, as configured by the user, or there is no OSC messaging information. The command is set/show ochm-<name>, in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode; only label, admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock) and alarm-report-control (allowed default, or inhibited) are settable. direction reports ingress or egress but only egress is currently supported, and for egress power-actual should be calibrated at the DWDM Line port output at the same reference point where the target power is defined. power-actual of -99 dBm means the power is not yet measured (measurement is performed by the OCM at the DGE2 card) or no power is detected. target-actual-power (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99) and attenuation-actual (0..55 dB) apply to HSC OLS nodes.
